quotes.text: We conclude the prohibition and fees were necessary to achieve the purpose of creating a uniform plan for the development and operation of the condominium project.

quotes.text: In neither the Salvation Army case nor the instant case was there any testimony of that character; in fact, the evidence shows that there was no advertising of the dormitory facilities in any of the five buildings here involved, and no complaints were heard from hotels or boarding houses that the dormitories were in competition with them.
Having thus disposed of the problem of the dormitories and food service facilities, the incidental problem of bowling alleys, barber shops, and businessmen's health clubs is easily resolved.

The permanent classification included all those who occupied the rooms for two weeks or more and paid rent-on a weekly basis; transients being those whose occupancy was less than two weeks and who paid on a daily basis.

E.holding_summary: The court held that YMCA dormitory and food-service facilities, though occupied by paying residents (some 'transient' for under two weeks, most 'permanent' for two weeks or more), were tax-exempt because their actual use was primarily charitable rather than commercial lodging. The court distinguished the case from an earlier ruling taxing a YMCA's dormitory that competed with avowedly commercial lodging houses, finding no comparable competition, advertising, or profit here.

E.name: Scottish American Mortgage Co. v. Milner

quotes.text: Any temporary renting would not defeat the homestead right.
Any temporary renting would not defeat the homestead right.

E.holding_summary: The Court of Civil Appeals held that a homeowner's temporary rental of a second house on his homestead lot to a tenant did not, as a matter of law, defeat the homestead exemption as to that house. An owner is entitled to a reasonable time after purchase to occupy the whole of a homestead lot, and temporary renting of part of it pending consolidation of the buildings does not conclusively show abandonment. Whether the renting was temporary (and thus consistent with continued homestead use) or evidenced a permanent commercial diversion was a fact question for the jury.

E.name: Peters v. Kelly

quotes.text: This evidence did not show a hiring of the yard adjacent to the house, and the stairway and the landing, together with the rooms, but only a hiring of the rooms themselves.
Having retained such control, it became her duty to exercise reasonable care to keep .the stairway and landing in suitable repair for use.

E.holding_summary: A landlord let three rooms of a rear tenement house to a tenant, with access by an outside stairway and landing not included in the letting. Because only the rooms themselves were hired, the landlord retained control of the stairway and landing and owed a duty of reasonable care to keep them in repair. The dismissal of a visitor's negligence complaint, for supposed lack of proof of retained control, was reversed.
